claims.text: Process fairness can be measured by estimating the degree to which people consider various features to be fair to use when making an important legal decision.
Process fairness can be achieved with little cost to outcome fairness.
Removing features that cause public discomfort leads to an unavoidable loss of prediction accuracy.

evidence.description: Process fairness can be measured by estimating the degree to which people consider various features to be fair to use when making an important legal decision.
Our empirical analysis suggests that process fairness may be achieved with little cost to outcome fairness.
Our empirical analysis suggests that ... some loss of accuracy is unavoidable.

methodologies.name: Process fairness estimation via feature selection
methodologies.description: Estimating public discomfort with decision-making features and evaluating the impact of removing uncomfortable features on model accuracy and outcome fairness.

limitations.text: Achieving process fairness through feature removal incurs an unavoidable loss of prediction accuracy.
Prior works focus on outcome fairness of decisions rather than considering the fairness of the decision-making process itself.
